MANILA, Philippines – The Senate impeachment court on Friday, November 20, ordered Vice President Sara Duterte‘s spokesperson, Paolo Panelo, to explain remarks accusing senator-judges of undermining the credibility of a defense witness.

The order came after Senator-judge Erwin Tulfo moved to issue a show-cause order against Panelo on the 45th day of Duterte’s impeachment trial, saying the lawyer-spokesperson’s comments showed disrespect toward the court.

“He’s not a party to this case but he is the spokesperson of the Vice President. Is this appropriate?” Tulfo said. “You are the spokesperson of the Vice President on trial and then, you will comment on senator-judges and the impeachment court. It seems like you have no respect [for] the impeachment court.”
Impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero said Panelo is not covered by Rule 18, or the sub judice rule, because he is not a party to the impeachment case.
However, the court may still cite him for contempt under the suppletory application of Rule 71 of the Rules of Court.
“Therefore, [he is] susceptible to any orders that this court may issue as against him in relation to speech or action made by him in connection with this impeachment court,” he said.
Escudero approved Tulfo’s motion and directed the Clerk of Court to issue the order.
Panelo earlier accused some senator-judges of showing bias and “appearing to act as lawyers for the prosecution” during their interjections with defense witness lawyer Rainer dela Fuente.
“Yes, based on the line of questioning from the senator-judges, those are actually questions that the prosecution should be asking, not the senator-judges,” said Panelo.
“It seemed like they were lawyering for the prosecution. Does the vice president feel that? No, that’s based on my personal opinion as an observer today,” he said.
Defense lawyer Michael Poa said it would not affect the defense’s strategy if Panelo gets a contempt citation.

“There are different rules for the defense. If it is a member of our team, they will be covered by the sub judice rule and I think the presiding officer clearly stated that Panelo is not covered. That’s why they are using Rule 71 of the Rules of Court. That is the prerogative of the court,” Poa told reporters.
“Let us just wait for him to respond and we’ll see how the impeachment court appreciates,” he said.
Duterte’s spokesperson took to social media to respond to the order, saying he would formally respond to the order “within the period provided upon receipt.”

“I welcome the opportunity to demonstrate that my comments were fair, made in good faith, and did not impede, obstruct, or degrade the administration of justice, and are thus constitutionally protected. I will formally respond to the Show Cause Order within the period provided upon receipt,” said Panelo. – Rappler.com
